record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: For Euclidean R^d, d>=2, what is the Steiner ratio, the infimum over finite point sets of Steiner-tree length divided by minimum-spanning-tree length? In the plane, is the value sqrt(3)/2 attained by an equilateral triangle?

evidence.quote: Question 2.4. What is the Steiner ratio in R^d,d≥2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\geq 2$ and a finite point set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, let $\mathrm{MST}(A)$ denote the length (sum of Euclidean edge lengths) of a minimum spanning tree of $A$, and let $\mathrm{SMT}(A)$ denote the length of a Steiner minimal tree on $A$ (the infimum of total Euclidean length over all finite connected graphs in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that contain $A$ among their vertices; equivalently, over all finite trees in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose vertex set contains $A$). Define the Steiner ratio in $\mathbb{R}^d$ by
$$\rho_d \;=\; \inf_{A}\, \frac{\mathrm{SMT}(A)}{\mathrm{MST}(A)},$$
where the infimum is taken over all finite subsets $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|A|\geq 2$.

(a) Determine $\rho_d$ for every $d\geq 2$.

(b) In the planar case $d=2$, decide whether $\rho_2 = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, the value attained on the vertex set of an equilateral triangle.
artifact.status_search_result: The Gilbert–Pollak conjecture asserts $\rho_2 = \sqrt{3}/2$. A 1990 proof attempt by Du and Hwang was later shown to contain serious gaps (Ivanov–Tuzhilin, 2012), and the conjecture is widely regarded as still open in the plane. The exact value of $\rho_d$ for $d\geq 3$ is also unknown; only bounds are available.

status_evidence.title: The Steiner Ratio Gilbert–Pollak Conjecture Is Still Open
status_evidence.snippet: Ivanov and Tuzhilin argue that the Du–Hwang proof contains serious gaps and the conjecture remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The planar Steiner ratio conjecture (value sqrt(3)/2) is still open.

status_evidence.title: Gilbert–Pollak conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The proof suggested by Du and Hwang in 1990 contains serious gaps; the conjecture's status is disputed/open.
status_evidence.claim: The Du–Hwang proof has gaps; status of the conjecture is open.
